title: Reconcile subtoken mappings and chat-schema delimiters during model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: New model manifests being onboarded sometimes declare tokenizer variants and chat template delimiters that produce different subtokenization for role markers (e.g., "User:" vs "<|user|>") across provider-provided tokenizers. This causes edge-case prompt truncation, misaligned KV cache keys, and degraded streaming boundaries in the serving runtime. The onboarding pipeline currently performs a basic tokenizer match check but does not reconcile subtoken mappings, nor does it publish a tokenizer fingerprint to the model manifest. As a result, downstream performance profiles and compatibility labels in the Console can be inaccurate and rollouts can fail when the runtime selects a variant with incompatible delimiters.

Goal: Implement a compatibility reconciliation step in the onboarding pipeline that: 1) computes a tokenizer fingerprint and canonical subtoken mapping for the model; 2) validates chat template delimiter equivalence and produces a deterministic shim when mappings differ; 3) publishes a compatibility report and updated performance profile only after reconciled tokenization and template tests pass. This ticket covers engineering work to add the reconciliation logic, test coverage, and a phased rollout plan with telemetry to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline generates 'tokenizer_fingerprint' and 'subtoken_map_v1' fields in model manifest for every new model
Compatibility step runs unit tests that assert semantic equivalence of role delimiters across common templates (chat, assistant, system) for 95% of sample prompts
A deterministic shim (token-sequence rewrite) is emitted when delimiter differences are detected and validated; runtime honors shim when model.version_pin includes 'allow_shim'
Performance profile publishing is gated behind successful tokenization reconciliation checks
E2E canary with 5% traffic shows no increase in prompt truncation errors or KV cache misses after rollout
tasks: Extend model-manifest schema to include tokenizer_fingerprint, tokenizer_version_hint, subtoken_map_v1
Implement reconciliation worker that runs tokenizer mapping, delimiter equivalence tests, and emits shim artifacts
Add integration tests that simulate common delimiter/punctuation edge-cases and assert KV cache key stability
Wire compatibility report into Console model page and onboarding logs
Add feature flag 'onboarding.tokenizer_reconcile' to gate rollout
Coordinate with model-onboarding docs owner to update onboarding checklist and PR template
implementation_notes: Design: The reconciliation worker will run in the onboarding pipeline (step 3). It will load the model-provided tokenizer (or a pinned tokenizer from our catalog), compute a stable hash of the tokenizer config and vocabulary (tokenizer_fingerprint), then run a canonical prompt suite (from /onboarding/canonical-prompts) to derive a mapping of role tokens to subtoken sequences. If mappings mismatch expectations, the worker will try to synthesize a minimal shim that rewrites incoming prompts or chat templates to the model's canonical role tokens. We prefer rewrites over runtime code-paths to keep runtime simple. The shim format is JSONL and includes a deterministic fingerprint and revert rule. We will add a small deterministic validator in the runtime that accepts the shim only if the model manifest contains "allow_shim":true and the shim fingerprint matches. Rollback: a negative canary will flip the feature flag and revert manifests for affected models. Telemetry: emit 'onboarding.tokenizer.delta' metric with sample counts and 'shim.applied' boolean.
tests: Unit: tokenizer fingerprinting and subtoken_map generation (100% coverage for mapping functions)
Integration: end-to-end onboarding pipeline test using sample models with known delimiter differences (3 variants)
E2E: canary rollout to runtime with synthetic traffic measuring KV cache hit rate and truncation rate
Regression: add fuzz corpus of user messages to catch delimiter-induced off-by-one tokenization bugs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature flag enabled only on onboarding-staging; run full pipeline and verify manifests. Phase 1 (canary): enable for 10% of new model onboards, publish compatibility report to Console and monitor 'onboarding.tokenizer.delta' and downstream 'runtime.kv_miss_rate' for 72 hours. Phase 2 (gradual): increase to 50% after 7 days if stable. Phase 3 (all): enable by default and require compatibility checks for published performance profiles. If any metric crosses thresholds, roll back via flag and revert manifests using the tracked bootstrap commit.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11 - Miguel Santos: Initial spike complete. Prototype generates tokenizer fingerprint and basic subtoken map for GPT-style and llama-style tokenizers.

2025-02-14 - Aisha Kapoor: Wrote design doc outlining shim format and validator rules (see links). Decided to prefer prompt-rewrite shim over runtime tokenization patching to minimize performance risk.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Santos: Integration tests added for 3 delimiter variants; two cases detected where role marker subtokens cause KV-key mismatch. Generated candidate shims and verified round-trip equivalence locally.
2025-02-22 - Jordan Lee (Review): Code review feedback posted on PR #4832 to tighten fingerprinting canonicalization and add an additional fuzz test. Assigned Miguel to address comments.
notes_for_pm: PM should review the compatibility report UI copy and decide whether to expose 'shim details' to customers or only surfacing a summary. Also coordinate with Solutions Engineering for any enterprise customers that require explicit tokenizer version pinning in their manifests.
